I wanted to ask the moderator a yes/no question, such as "does a second copy of my role exist?", but no such channel exists.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Day 4 Dave trial came back 2 Guilty and 2 Innocent, while several players publicly said they had voted Guilty. The public record of who said what was contradictory, and nothing in the announced totals could resolve it. Players also repeated identical claim blocks several times in a single Day, which made the public log noisy and harder to read. Carol's Night 2 result said she was attacked by a Katana and a Serial Killer. That matched the charm reports from both Kitsune claimants, so the two charm stories were consistent with each other, which made it hard to tell which Kitsune was lying. In fact neither was lying.
answers.suggestions: 1) Post whether roles can repeat, or how many duplicates exist, before Day 2. This would have prevented my main mistake. 2) Post trial totals with the number of voters and let each voter see a private receipt that can be checked against the total. 3) Let a Kitsune's release be announced as "a charm released on X" without the cause, so the cause is not stated publicly before it lands. 4) Show a short running ledger of claims, night results and votes in the public log, so players don't have to reconstruct it from memory. 5) State in the rules whether a Kitsune's release counts as an action for role-block and visit purposes.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) Two Kitsune charms on one player (Night 2: Erin and Heidi both charmed Carol, who was hit by Frank's Standard Katana and Dave's Strong Serial Killer attack). The Kitsune text says the charm "acts before any other protection" and swallows one attack "chosen at random if there are several". It doesn't say what happens when two charms land on the same player. Can both swallow the same attack? Does the second charm see only what's left? Is the order random or by seat? I ruled that each charm swallows a different attack: I picked at random which charm went first, it took a random attack, and the second charm took the one left. That fit Carol's notification ("attacked twice, survived both"), but the rules should say so.
2) Whether a Kitsune release is a visit. The rules say the charm defaults to a visit. They don't say whether releasing a held attack is a visit, an Astral Visit or neither. It didn't matter in this game (no Tracker, Lookout or Veteran alive on Night 3), but it would matter with those roles.
3) A held attack when the Kitsune dies. Erin died on Night 3 still holding the swallowed Katana attack. I treated it as lost, but no rule covers this.
4) What a player killed by a released attack is told. A survivor "is told it came from that cause's role", but nothing covers someone who dies of one. I told Erin "attacked (Serial Killer) and died", following the death announcement's cause. That's consistent, but it's an extrapolation.
5) Whether a released attack counts as an Attack made by the Kitsune or by the original attacker. This matters for Bloodhound counts and for an Avenger's retaliation. Not relevant here, but undefined.
answers.missing_information:
1) The moderator log doesn't show each player's actual nomination and trial votes, only the totals. On Day 4, Alice publicly said she voted Guilty in Dave's first trial, and her later claim ledger said Innocent on both Dave trials. Grace first said Guilty, then Innocent. With a 2–2 result and Heidi Guilty and Dave Innocent, at least one of them misstated their vote, and I couldn't check which from my view. As moderator I should see the per-player ballots.
2) There was no state panel for held Kitsune attacks, token counts or the Katana holder. I had to rebuild from the log who held which swallowed attack and at what level and cause (Erin: Standard Katana; Heidi: Strong SK).
3) The list of each player's notifications from each night wasn't in one place. That made it harder to check that every attacked player got exactly one correct message.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1) I wanted to look up the actual votes so I could confirm the 2–2 and 3–1 totals against what players said.
2) There was no tool to log a rules interpretation, such as the double-Kitsune ruling, so that later nights would follow it consistently.
3) I couldn't send a neutral clarification about how two charms resolve. Carol's message said only "survived both", and the players then spent all of Day 3 arguing whether two Kitsunes could both be real.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) The result templates weren't consistent from night to night:
   - Night 1 Sheriff: "You investigated Dave tonight. Result: Not Evil."
   - Night 2 Sheriff: "Night 2 result: Erin is Not Evil…" with the attack notice folded in.
   - Dave's kill results: "Your attack on Bob succeeded." / "You attacked Carol tonight. Your attack succeeded." / "Your attack succeeded: Alice was killed."
   The same events should get the same wording.
2) Players leaked hidden information and the system did nothing to stop it:
   - Day 2: Alice said publicly "Dave survived a Katana attack last night". Only the Yakuza and Dave knew that, and nobody noticed.
   - Day 3: Frank wrote "the Katana I aimed at Carol" and "my Katana on Carol failed", which got him hanged.
   - Day 4: Dave's claim-ledger entry said his N1–N3 results "were my own attacks", which nearly got him hanged.
   These are player-side mistakes, but the claim tool accepted and published a self-incriminating summary. That suggests the claim tool is also writing from players' private role context.
3) Heidi's Night 3 release on Erin was announced as "killed by Serial Killer". That's correct by the rules, but it made the Village believe the SK had made three or four kills, and it pinned Heidi's kill on Dave. The design intends this, but it strongly confuses deduction.
4) Heidi's claim "N3 released SK, killed Erin (fake Kitsune)" asserted something she couldn't know, and it contradicted her own public statement a moment earlier that two real Kitsunes were possible. That's player inconsistency, not a moderator bug.
5) Day 2 ran its full length with no nomination. Most messages were near-identical "waiting for Carol's check" filler, which used up a lot of turns for nothing.
answers.suggestions:
1) Add a rule for multiple Kitsune charms on one target. For example: "Charms resolve in random order; each swallows a different attack if one is left; a charm with nothing left swallows nothing." Also state whether a release is a visit, what happens to a held attack when its Kitsune dies, and what a player killed by a released attack is told.
2) Give the moderator a private ballot view (who voted Yes/No and Guilty/Innocent) and a state panel showing the Katana holder, tokens, held Kitsune attacks, traps and marks.
3) Use fixed templates for all results ("You investigated X: Not Evil", "Your attack on X succeeded/failed").
4) Have the claim tool build summaries only from what the player chooses to claim, so it can't paraphrase hidden role details. Also warn players before they post public text containing first-person faction words ("my Katana", "my attacks").
5) Consider letting players end a round early, or making repeated near-identical filler cost more, so stalled Days like Day 2 resolve faster.
6) Allow a logged moderator ruling note, so interpretations stay consistent and can be reviewed.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A held swallowed attack is worthless once you die, so release it on the first night you suspect you may be targeted or exposed, and pick a target whose death you can justify. I died on Night 3 still holding a Katana I never released.

Don't spend two charms on the same player. My Night 1 and Night 2 charms both went on Carol, which gave one fact-set instead of two. Spread charms over likely targets (claimed investigators, the player who survived an unexplained attack) so each night adds information.

When two players claim the same unique-feeling role, look for a victim or third party whose own notifications corroborate one claim. Carol's N2 double-attack notification matched both Kitsune stories, so it proved the events but not who was lying. Ask for the claim that adds a checkable detail, like the exact level and cause on release.

Write down every stated vote the moment it's announced and compare it to the totals before any nomination. The Dave trial mismatch (2-2 against several 'Guilty' claims) exposed a false vote claim, but only after two hangs had been driven by wording-level reads.

Don't hang on a single phrase or wording slip (Frank, then Grace). A hang needs a mechanical fit such as a Katana victim's visitor list, a Sheriff read, or a vote count. Otherwise the Yakuza can convert hang pressure into a Village-on-Village execution.
Many turns repeated 'no nomination from me' and the same request, which costs budget without adding information. Spend budget on the one claim or vote question that moves the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Dying with unused shots is the usual failure (Vigilante tip, general 'dead players spend nothing')
tips_feedback.why: It described my own failure exactly: I died holding a released-but-unfired attack, so the swallowed Katana was lost with me.

tips_feedback.tip: Totals can be altered; first have everyone re-check their vote reminder, and treat mismatches as leads
tips_feedback.why: The 2-2 Dave trial count and the Grace vote-claim flip came out of comparing stated votes with announced totals, which exposed the false vote claim.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits (an Evil read against a claim that can't explain it), not leans, PM trails or wording
tips_feedback.why: Village players hanged Frank and then Grace on wording and PM patterns, which is the very thing the tip warns against. The tip was right, but the Village didn't follow it, and the Yakuza-side pattern worked against them.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets and vary them
tips_feedback.why: The game shows no protector was ever revealed, and Dave survived a Standard Katana with no named Medic. The tip assumes a Medic exists, but here the survival came from an unexplained source, so the tip's implied protection model didn't apply.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A visit that lines up with a death is strong evidence. Bob's Tracker result showed Dave visiting Bob on Night 1, and Bob then died to a Serial Killer that night. The Village never cross-checked that, so Dave survived to the end. When a Tracker or Lookout result sits on a victim, check the visitor first, before debating claims.

Don't hang on a single phrase or wording slip. Frank, Grace and Dave were each nominated over one word or a vote-count dispute. Good players were executed while the real killer stayed alive. Require a mechanical reason, such as a result, a death cause, or a verified vote total, before voting Guilty.

Check announced vote totals against stated votes before the next nomination. The 2-2 Dave count was used as a weapon by several players, and the Village spent days arguing over it instead of over the real evidence. Ask each voter to restate their Guilty or Innocent vote once, and then drop the topic.

Unexplained survivors are suspects. Dave survived a Standard Katana on Night 1 with no protector named, and that matched Standard Defense. Serial Killers have Standard Defense innately. Treat any player who survives an attack with no protector as a lead to test, not as a clear.

A charm on a player who later dies to the attack it swallowed is confirmed information. Only the real Kitsune has a unique charm story that matches deaths. If two players claim the same role, test each claim against the next death cause before hanging either one.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive).
tips_feedback.why: This was the correct diagnosis. Late in the game the Village reasoned that the Serial Killer was alive from the death causes, and that narrowed the suspects. It came too late to save Good players.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The principle is sound, and the game showed the cost of ignoring it. Frank and Grace were hanged on wording and vote-count disputes, which were not mechanical evidence. Following the tip earlier would have protected Good players.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current with past results.
tips_feedback.why: My will named the Tracker lead that pointed at Dave. The lead was correct, but nobody acted on it, so the benefit was lost. The tip is good, but a will only helps if the village reads it.

Check whether both stories fit real night events before calling either one fake. Here both Kitsune charm stories matched real attacks, and the Village wrongly treated one as false.

Before a hang, reconcile every announced total with each player's stated vote. A mismatch can be a miscount or a self-correction, not a lie. Grace was executed after flip-flopping her vote claim on Dave's first trial, which turned out to be an honest miscount. Ask for the reminder explanation before the next nomination.

Wording evidence is strong when it's a first-person action from a player claiming a role that can't do it, but weak when it's a single phrase in a defense. Separate these cases before hanging. Frank's slip was real, but the same standard applied to Dave and Grace produced hangs on weaker evidence.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, deal with the protector first, or suspect innate Defense and push a hang instead.
tips_feedback.why: I inferred Dave had Standard defense after his Night 1 Katana survival, which correctly explained why later Katana votes against him were useless and pointed the team at him as the SK.

tips_feedback.tip: Treat mismatches as leads, not proof (ballots are secret; keep a notepad of stated votes and totals).
tips_feedback.why: The 2-2 Dave trial mismatch was a real lead, but Grace's self-correction was an honest miscount. Village treated the mismatch as proof of a lie, which contributed to executing a Village player.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's first-person Katana wording was actually true (he was Yakuza), so the wording case was correct; but the Village repeated the wording logic against Dave and Grace where it didn't hold, so the tip only helps when applied consistently.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death and list unexplained survivors.
tips_feedback.why: The Katana-survival and SK-kill pattern pointed at Dave, but the Village couldn't act on it before the SK won, since hangs were stuck on phrase-level disputes and the last two players couldn't agree.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill roles whose future results narrow you (Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller, Coroner, blockers), not one whose result is already public.
tips_feedback.why: This tip isn't really about the Yakuza here: the SK, not any investigator, was the real threat. Dave's kills on Bob, Carol, Erin, Heidi and Alice were what decided the game, and the tip gave no guidance for hunting a Standard-defense Neutral.

lessons.tip: A visit that lines up with a death is strong evidence. Bob's Tracker result showed Dave visiting Bob on Night 1, and Bob then died to a Serial Killer that night. The Village never cross-checked that, so Dave survived to the end. When a Tracker or Lookout result sits on a victim, check the visitor first, before debating claims.

Don't hang on a single phrase or wording slip. Frank, Grace and Dave were each nominated over one word or a vote-count dispute. Good players were executed while the real killer stayed alive. Require a mechanical reason, such as a result, a death cause, or a verified vote total, before voting Guilty.

Check announced vote totals against stated votes before the next nomination. The 2-2 Dave count was used as a weapon by several players, and the Village spent days arguing over it instead of over the real evidence. Ask each voter to restate their Guilty or Innocent vote once, and then drop the topic.

Unexplained survivors are suspects. Dave survived a Standard Katana on Night 1 with no protector named, and that matched Standard Defense. Serial Killers have Standard Defense innately. Treat any player who survives an attack with no protector as a lead to test, not as a clear.

A charm on a player who later dies to the attack it swallowed is confirmed information. Only the real Kitsune has a unique charm story that matches deaths. If two players claim the same role, test each claim against the next death cause before hanging either one.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive).
tips_feedback.why: This was the correct diagnosis. Late in the game the Village reasoned that the Serial Killer was alive from the death causes, and that narrowed the suspects. It came too late to save Good players.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The principle is sound, and the game showed the cost of ignoring it. Frank and Grace were hanged on wording and vote-count disputes, which were not mechanical evidence. Following the tip earlier would have protected Good players.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep your will current with past results.
tips_feedback.why: My will named the Tracker lead that pointed at Dave. The lead was correct, but nobody acted on it, so the benefit was lost. The tip is good, but a will only helps if the village reads it.

lessons.tip: A Not Evil read on a Neutral killer proves nothing. Serial Killers and Arsonists read Not Evil to the Sheriff. Before trusting a clean read, ask whether the target could be a Neutral killer, and cross-check it against the death causes and the Standard-Defense survivors.

A player who survives a Standard Katana with no named protector probably has innate Standard Defense (Serial Killer), not a Medic. Look for the Neutral killer among the survivors of Standard attacks before assuming a Good protector exists.

Do not hang Village players on a single phrase or wording slip. Hanging Frank was right only because his phrase lined up with a real Katana night. Grace's hang on phrases killed a Village player, and the Village was then down to two living Good players. Ask for a mechanical contradiction first.

With an even number of voters a tie is not a majority, so the accused is Innocent. Count the voters before pushing a hang, and when the total reads 2-2, ask who actually voted what before the next nomination.

Posting a claim with a planned next-night target made me the target that night. Publicly stated check targets, and the claim itself, invite a Katana or Serial Killer hit. Consider holding the target back, and have a protector or a second claimant ready before you announce.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators usually do best posting night, target and exact result as soon as it bears on a vote
tips_feedback.why: I posted my Sheriff claim and a planned Night 2 check target. The Serial Killer and Katana both hit me on Night 2 and killed me on Night 3, so the public plan was predictable and got me targeted.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording
tips_feedback.why: This held against the Frank wording and PM-trail cases. The Grace nomination on phrases was the exception, and it cost the Village a Good player, so the tip is right in principle but needs to be applied consistently.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets
tips_feedback.why: The Serial Killer and the Katana both hit me on Night 2 and I survived both, but no protector was named. Standard-Defense Neutrals also survive Standard hits, so a survived Katana does not prove a Medic exists.

lessons.applies_to: Serial Killer or any Neutral killer
lessons.tip: Kill claimed investigators (Sheriff, Seer, Tracker) early, and keep killing the strongest remaining claimant each night. Their results are the main threat, and a Village that cannot verify claims will stall or hang its own.

lessons.applies_to: Serial Killer or any Neutral killer
lessons.tip: With two players alive, a hanging needs both votes. Vote No on every nomination and make the other survivor look like the threat. Then use the night kill on the last other player to win alone.

lessons.applies_to: Serial Killer or any Neutral killer
lessons.tip: Let the Village hang its own. Quietly backing pushes against town-looking players on weak phrase-level evidence costs you nothing, while publicly defending the accused makes you the next suspect.
Do not claim a role with first-person action wording ("my Katana", "my attacks") unless you have it. Players treat such slips as a Yakuza or Neutral tell and hang on them.
Before any hang, have each player restate their exact vote, then compare the announced totals. Unexplained extra Guilty counts are the reliable lead, not the wording of a defence.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The Village ignored it and hanged Frank and Grace on single phrases and a vote miscount. Their hangs removed Village players, which helped my Serial Killer win.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death and list unwatched Vanilla claimants.
tips_feedback.why: The Village never used the death causes to identify the Serial Killer. Dave's Katana survival was mistaken for a Standard-defense tell, and the actual SK was never named, so the tip did not help the town here.

tips_feedback.tip: Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wants it, and keep Guilty votes to a bare majority.
tips_feedback.why: The Village kept hanging its own on flimsy cases with no check on who was pushing. Unchecked hangs cleared the town of Village players while the Serial Killer stayed hidden.

lessons.tip: A held swallowed attack is worthless once you die, so release it on the first night you suspect you may be targeted or exposed, and pick a target whose death you can justify. I died on Night 3 still holding a Katana I never released.

Don't spend two charms on the same player. My Night 1 and Night 2 charms both went on Carol, which gave one fact-set instead of two. Spread charms over likely targets (claimed investigators, the player who survived an unexplained attack) so each night adds information.

When two players claim the same unique-feeling role, look for a victim or third party whose own notifications corroborate one claim. Carol's N2 double-attack notification matched both Kitsune stories, so it proved the events but not who was lying. Ask for the claim that adds a checkable detail, like the exact level and cause on release.

Write down every stated vote the moment it's announced and compare it to the totals before any nomination. The Dave trial mismatch (2-2 against several 'Guilty' claims) exposed a false vote claim, but only after two hangs had been driven by wording-level reads.

Don't hang on a single phrase or wording slip (Frank, then Grace). A hang needs a mechanical fit such as a Katana victim's visitor list, a Sheriff read, or a vote count. Otherwise the Yakuza can convert hang pressure into a Village-on-Village execution.
Many turns repeated 'no nomination from me' and the same request, which costs budget without adding information. Spend budget on the one claim or vote question that moves the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Dying with unused shots is the usual failure (Vigilante tip, general 'dead players spend nothing')
tips_feedback.why: It described my own failure exactly: I died holding a released-but-unfired attack, so the swallowed Katana was lost with me.

tips_feedback.tip: Totals can be altered; first have everyone re-check their vote reminder, and treat mismatches as leads
tips_feedback.why: The 2-2 Dave trial count and the Grace vote-claim flip came out of comparing stated votes with announced totals, which exposed the false vote claim.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits (an Evil read against a claim that can't explain it), not leans, PM trails or wording
tips_feedback.why: Village players hanged Frank and then Grace on wording and PM patterns, which is the very thing the tip warns against. The tip was right, but the Village didn't follow it, and the Yakuza-side pattern worked against them.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana: guard likely targets and vary them
tips_feedback.why: The game shows no protector was ever revealed, and Dave survived a Standard Katana with no named Medic. The tip assumes a Medic exists, but here the survival came from an unexplained source, so the tip's implied protection model didn't apply.

lessons.tip: Scrub first-person action wording from day chat. A Vanilla Villager saying 'my Katana on Carol failed' while repeating a teammate's claim was enough to get me hanged. If you must reference a night event, use the wording a Village player would use, and make sure it matches your claimed role.

Two players claiming the same role is not proof that one is lying. Duplicate roles can both be real (here, both Kitsunes were real). Before concluding that someone is a liar, check whether the role could appear twice and whether the two claims are actually incompatible.

Do not hang on a phrase or a wording slip. Frank and Grace were both executed on single-sentence readings, and the Village ended up with only Dave, the Serial Killer, left alive. Require a mechanical contradiction (a result that conflicts with a visit or a death) before a hang.

State your vote exactly once, and reconcile it against the announced totals. Several players publicly misstated their trial votes, which created a 2-2 count nobody could resolve and made every later vote look suspicious.

Before choosing a Katana target, check whether the target is a likely protected investigator. Our Katana failed on Dave (N1) and on Carol (N2, likely protected), and each failure cost us information and credibility, while the Serial Killer kept killing freely. Consider whether a Neutral killer in the game changes which targets are worth it.

tips_feedback.tip: Plan only in night chat; daytime teammate PMs are visible to all.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and I kept our coordination in the Yakuza night chat, so no daytime PM ever exposed us as a pair.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree distinct cover claims before Day 2 that fit your tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: Alice and I both claimed Vanilla with no night action, which is bland and hard to defend when Village asks for detail. The first-person Katana slip I made came from trying to explain our night, and it got me executed.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: This is correct advice, and the Village ignored it on Days 3 and 4. Had they followed it, they would have had more time to identify the Serial Killer before only two players remained.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana; guard likely targets such as claimed investigators.
tips_feedback.why: Carol survived my Katana on N2 and was protected or otherwise unhit by it, which removed a Yakuza kill and gave the Village a surviving Sheriff for a night.

lessons.tip: A Kitsune's released attack keeps the cause of the attack it swallowed, so a 'Serial Killer' death on a later night can be a Kitsune release rather than a live Serial Killer. Before assuming a new killer is alive, check whether a Kitsune charm swallowed that cause earlier.

Two players can share a role, and two Kitsune claims can both be true. Don't eliminate one claimant on a 'they must be fake' argument. Check which claimed events deaths and visits independently match, and weigh both claims until something separates them.

A Not Evil alignment read on a player who survived an unexplained Standard-level attack is a lead, not a clearance. Serial Killers and Arsonists read Not Evil and have Standard Defense, so ask which Neutral killer explains the survival before counting the read as clean.

Check your own vote reminder before you state it publicly, and don't correct a public vote claim after the fact. A wrong stated vote that is later reversed reads as a lie, and it made me the main suspect even though I was Village.

Don't nominate on a single wording slip, and don't coordinate a hang after a burst of private messages with one player. Others read that as a bloc. Build the case on a result that lines up with deaths or visits, and state it in public chat before the vote.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret: keep a notepad of each player's stated vote and treat mismatches as leads.
tips_feedback.why: The 2-2 count on Dave's first trial exposed that someone had misstated their vote, and the table kept pressure on the misreport. It was my own misreport, so the tip correctly flagged me but could not stop the chain of hangs.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits, not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: I pushed nominations on Frank and then Dave and Alice on single phrases, and that is exactly what the tip warns against. Frank was in fact Yakuza, so the hang worked by luck, while the same method on Dave and Alice nearly sent the Village to a loss.

tips_feedback.tip: Free Standard protection stops the Katana, and the Katana holder reads Not Evil that night.
tips_feedback.why: The Katana-holder Not Evil note stopped Carol's Not Evil read on Frank's or Alice's night from being treated as a clean result, and the Standard-defense note correctly pointed at the Serial Killer's innate Standard Defense on Dave.

lessons.tip: Don't spend your first fox charm on an arbitrary player. Charm the player most likely to be attacked (a claimed investigator, or the player whose death would hurt you). My N1 charm on Alice caught nothing, while the N2 charm on Carol caught a real Strong Serial Killer attack, which is what made the held attack useful.

Two players can share a role claim and both be telling the truth. Kitsune Erin and Kitsune Heidi were both real. Before you call a rival claim fake, check it mechanically: a swallowed attack's level and cause must match a real attack that night on that player. Don't release a held attack (a kill) on someone you only dislike.

A Serial Killer has innate Standard Defense. A Standard Katana that fails on a player with no named protector is evidence for a Neutral SK, not for that player being Village. Use survival-with-no-protector as a lead toward the SK.

Don't convict on one wording slip or a disputed vote count. The Village hanged Frank on a phrase and then Grace on a disputed count, leaving the Serial Killer with an easy path. When only 3 or 4 Village remain, each hang on weak evidence is a gift to a Neutral killer.
Never announce tonight's night target or charm plan in public chat. I wrote 'tonight I'll lay my charm', and the Serial Killer killed me that night. A silent target keeps your night action useful.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid announcing tonight's target or token plans, even by PM, and avoid firm exact-role claims without a result
tips_feedback.why: I ignored it by saying I would lay my charm that night and post what it caught. The Serial Killer targeted me that same night, so the public plan made me the obvious kill and wasted the charm.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits (an Evil read against a claim that can't explain it...), not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: The table, including me, convicted Frank on a first-person wording slip and then Grace on a disputed vote count. Frank was Village, and the Village lost the votes it needed to stop the Serial Killer.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive).
tips_feedback.why: Reading the causes of death on Bob, Carol, Erin, Heidi and Alice showed a Serial Killer was alive. That narrowed the field to Dave, even though the table never managed to convict him.

summary: The Serial Killer (Dave) won alone, and both other factions made mistakes that let him. On Night 1 Dave killed the Tracker, Bob, and survived the Katana thanks to his innate Standard Defense. Carol's Sheriff check then read him Not Evil. Both of these fit a Serial Killer, but nobody acted on them until Day 4. Erin and Heidi were both real Kitsunes. Heidi called Erin a liar on the grounds that "I know my own role", even though roles can repeat. On Night 2 both Kitsunes charmed Carol, which saved her from the Katana and the SK. Then both of them were holding swallowed attacks, which meant neither could charm. On Night 3 Carol had no protection and died, and Heidi released her stored SK attack on Erin, killing a fellow Kitsune. Erin died still holding her stored Katana attack. On Day 3 Frank (Yakuza) wrote "my Katana on Carol failed" while claiming Vanilla, and the village rightly hanged him. Day 4 left four players: Alice (Yakuza), Dave (SK), Grace and Heidi (Village). The village came close to hanging Dave, but Grace voted Innocent by mistake after saying she'd vote Guilty, so the first trial tied 2-2. Her public correction made her look like a liar. Alice, the last Yakuza, then voted to save Dave and hang Grace. That was fatal for Alice: a Standard Katana can never kill a Serial Killer, so in a 1-on-1 he always wins. Dave killed Heidi on Night 4 and Alice on Night 5. If Alice had hanged Dave on Day 4, she would most likely have won with the Katana against two villagers. Day 2 was also wasted: about 8 rounds of everyone repeating "waiting for Carol's check".

lessons.tip: A duplicate claim of a non-unique role is not proof that one claimant is lying. Only Smuggler and Vulture are unique. Before calling a liar or acting on it, check whether both claims can be true together, for example whether both explain the same night's events.
lessons.evidence: Heidi said Erin's Kitsune claim was false because she knew her own role. On Night 2 their two charms on Carol swallowed a Katana attack and an SK attack, which matched Carol's report of surviving both. Heidi still released her held SK attack on Erin on Night 3, killing a real Village Kitsune, and only admitted the mistake on Day 4.

lessons.tip: When a Serial Killer is alive, take any chance to hang him, even if it means siding with villagers. Your Standard Katana can't get through his Standard Defense, but his Strong Attack kills any of you. If the game comes down to you and him, you lose. Count ahead: once the SK is gone, a lone Katana holder can usually block hangings and kill their way to a win.
lessons.evidence: On Day 4 Alice voted Guilty on Dave's first trial, then switched to Innocent on the second and to Guilty on the villager Grace. That left Alice and Dave alive. Her Katana couldn't hurt him, and he killed her on Night 5. If she had hanged Dave, it would have been Alice against Grace and Heidi, with no majority for the village to hang her.

lessons.tip: A player who survived the Katana with no protector claimed, and who reads Not Evil to a Sheriff, fits a Serial Killer. Add evasion about what he did at night and you have your best hang target. Make the case early, before the SK can thin the village.
lessons.evidence: Dave survived the Katana on Night 1 and read Not Evil to Carol. He also said his results were 'my own attacks, which I'm not sharing'. Nobody pushed this until Day 4, and by then the SK had killed Bob, Carol, Erin and later Heidi.

lessons.tip: In a small endgame, every vote decides the game. Check your vote reminder before you say how you voted, cast the vote you announced, and never state a vote you aren't sure of. Village: when one stated vote doesn't match the count, the likely explanation in a 4-player game is a single misclick. Treat it as a lead and question the person, not as grounds to hang them.
lessons.evidence: Grace nominated Dave and said she was voting Guilty, but cast Innocent, so the trial tied 2-2. She first said publicly she had voted Guilty and later 'corrected' it to Innocent. Heidi, Dave and Alice then hanged her for the mismatch, which handed the game to the SK.

lessons.tip: Keep your night perspective out of day chat entirely. Don't use first-person words about Katana actions or kill results. Before posting, reread your message from your fake role's point of view. One slip like this gets you hanged even with no other evidence.
lessons.evidence: Frank, claiming Vanilla, wrote 'the Katana I aimed at Carol' and 'my Katana on Carol failed'. Grace nominated him at once and he was hanged 5-2. Dave nearly went the same way with 'my own attacks'.

lessons.tip: While you hold a swallowed attack you can't protect anyone. Release it soon, on your best-supported suspect, so your charm is available again. Don't release it on a counterclaimant of your own role, and don't die still holding it. If two protectors exist, avoid both stacking on one target and then both being unable to protect.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2 both Kitsunes swallowed attacks on Carol. On Night 3 Erin did nothing and Heidi used her stored attack on Erin, so neither could charm. Carol, the confirmed-looking Sheriff, died to the Katana and the SK. Erin died with her stored Katana attack unused.

lessons.tip: If there's nothing new to say, stop posting, or use the time to ask specific questions and assign checks. Repeating 'no nomination, waiting for the check' through every round wastes budget and gives the hidden killers cover for a whole Day.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 every player posted some version of 'waiting for Carol's Day 3 check' for about 8 rounds. Nobody followed up on Dave's Not Evil read or on how the Katana target on Night 1 could have survived. Dave hid comfortably among them.

tips_feedback.tip: Check mechanics before calling a contradiction: actions are optional, roles can repeat, a role-block explains a missing result and a swap an odd one.
tips_feedback.why: The tip was right, and ignoring it was costly. Heidi treated a repeated Kitsune claim as a lie and killed Erin, a real Village Kitsune, on Night 3. Carol and Erin had correctly noted that two Kitsunes fit the Night 2 events.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical fits (an Evil read against a claim that can't explain it, elimination to one unexplained visitor, a broken claim), not leans, PM trails or wording.
tips_feedback.why: Alice (Yakuza) and Dave (SK) used the 'not wording' part to defend Frank and Dave and to attack Grace's 'phrase' cases. Both wording cases were correct: Frank's 'my Katana' was a real Yakuza slip, and Dave's 'my own attacks' was a real SK slip. A first-person action slip that contradicts a player's claim is a broken claim, and the village should treat it that way.

tips_feedback.tip: Hunt Neutral killers deliberately: read every cause of death (a Serial Killer attack or ignite proves one alive) and list unwatched Vanilla claimants and unexplained survivors.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 4 Grace and Heidi built the correct case on Dave's unexplained Katana survival and the SK causes of death. It nearly hanged the SK. It came too late to matter, and Grace's misvote undid it.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret: keep a notepad of each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own vote, ask for stated votes beforehand, and treat mismatches as leads, not proof.
tips_feedback.why: The vote tracking caught that Grace's stated Guilty didn't match the 2-2 count. But the village and the evil players treated the mismatch as proof, and Grace, an honest villager who had simply misclicked, was hanged on it. This decided the game for the SK. The tip's 'leads, not proof' warning was not followed.

tips_feedback.tip: Agree distinct cover claims before Day 2 that fit your tokens and real visits; switching when cornered, naming a Yakuza-only role or voicing night-chat knowledge usually gets you hanged.
tips_feedback.why: The game confirmed the tip. Frank spoke from his Katana holder's perspective while claiming Vanilla and was hanged on Day 3 for that alone.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, deal with the protector first, or suspect innate Defense and push a hang instead.
tips_feedback.why: The game confirmed the tip, though the Yakuza never acted on it. The Night 1 Katana failed against Dave's innate Defense. The Yakuza never pushed to hang him, and on Day 4 Alice voted to save him. That decided the game against the Yakuza.

issues.description: Night 2: Erin and Heidi (both real Kitsune) charmed Carol, who was hit by two non-Divine attacks (Frank's Standard Katana, Dave's Strong Serial Killer attack). The Kitsune text and R10 don't say how two charms on one player interact. The moderator flagged this and resolved the charms one after the other in random order, so each swallowed a different attack and Carol survived. Under a simultaneous reading, both charms could pick the same attack and Carol would die. The ruling decided whether Carol survived and was told both attackers, and it shaped the rest of the game. The rules should say whether stacked charms resolve one after the other or each draws independently.

Heidi (real Kitsune) said Erin's Kitsune claim must be false because 'I know my own role'. The setup note says roles may repeat, and Kitsune is not a unique role (R2). Acting on this mistake, Heidi used her held Serial Killer attack on Erin on Night 3, killing a fellow Village Kitsune. She partly admitted the error on Day 4 but then repeated the false claim in her trial message and her last will. Erin also said on Day 3 that 'Carol can't be charmed by two Kitsunes on one night', which the rules don't support (the gap above at most leaves how stacked charms resolve open).

Day 4: Grace nominated Dave, said publicly she would vote Guilty and asked Alice privately to vote Guilty, but her vote was counted Innocent. She then said publicly that she had voted Guilty and used the 2-2 count to nominate Alice, saying Alice's Guilty claim was the false one. Only later did she check her reminder and correct herself. Either the model misread or misentered its own vote, or a vote was missing and the harness defaulted it to Innocent. Either way, it led to Grace being hanged as the Village's last non-Kitsune. Worth checking whether her vote was actually submitted.

Two non-Village players revealed private information in public chat. Frank, claiming Vanilla Villager, wrote 'the Katana I aimed at Carol that night' and 'my Katana on Carol failed', and was hanged for it. Dave, claiming Vanilla Villager, set a claim saying his N1-N3 results were 'my own attacks'. This suggests the models mix up their private night results and role-based view with what is safe to say publicly.

On Day 3, Carol said surviving a Standard Katana meant either a Good protector such as a Medic covered her or the Katana was blocked, even though both claimed Kitsune said their charms swallowed attacks on her. Alice also said on Day 3 that Heidi's charm story 'only fits if someone protected Carol at Standard or Strong'. Both misread how the Kitsune's swallow works as protection.
